vars.prTitle: Don't cache empty role placeholders in RoleResolveUtil
vars.prBody: When a protocol mapper asks RoleResolveUtil for realm/client roles with createIfMissing=true, an empty Access object was written into the per-request resolved-roles cache. Subsequent mappers in the same request then see an (empty) realm_access/resource_access entry instead of null, which can end up as empty claims. This keeps the placeholder local to the caller and leaves the cached resolved roles untouched. Javadoc updated accordingly.
vars.goldenComments: [{"comment": "RoleResolveUtil.getResolvedRealmRoles/getResolvedClientRoles with createIfMissing=true no longer store the new Access in the per-request cached AccessToken. The callers that pass true do so precisely to mutate the cached roles so that later role mappers emit them: HardcodedRole.setClaim (services/.../protocol/oidc/mappers/HardcodedRole.java) calls getResolvedRealmRoles(..., true).addRole(role) / getResolvedClientRoles(..., appName, true).addRole(roleName), and RoleNameMapper.setClaim does the same for the renamed role. Both run before the role mappers (PRIORITY_HARDCODED_ROLE_MAPPER=20 / PRIORITY_ROLE_NAMES_MAPPER=10 < PRIORITY_ROLE_MAPPER=40), and UserRealmRoleMappingMapper/UserClientRoleMappingMapper read the cache with createIfMissing=false. When the user has no realm role (or no role of the target client), the role is now added to a throw-away object: hardcoded roles and renamed roles silently disappear from access tokens (and RoleNameMapper also removes the original role, so the user loses it entirely).", "severity": "High"}]
